newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FEDOROV SCORES FIVE GOALS IN RED WINGS' OVERTIME WIN.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FEDOROV SCORES FIVE GOALS IN RED WINGS' OVERTIME WIN.

text.p: Sergei Fedorov's fifth goal of the game at 2:39 of overtime lifted the Detroit Red Wings to a 5-4 victory over the Washington Capitals on Thursday.
"I'm still shaking, I'm so excited," said Fedorov. "This is wonderful."
The Russian centre added: "The puck was going in for me. I think all my shots went in."

Fedorov, whose previous career best was a four-goal game in a tie against the Kings in February 1995, was between the circles when he took a pass from defenceman Vladimir Konstantinov and beat Washington goaltender Jim Carey to the glove side.
"It was very exciting with that overtime goal because when you score you win, and you're done with the game," said Fedorov, who entered the game with just 12 goals and 25 points in 35 games.
Chris Osgood made 34 saves for Detroit and Carey finished with 28 saves for the Capitals.
Konstantiov had a career-high four assists and his first four-point game. Igor Larionov assisted on three of the goals.
In Ottawa, Alexei Yashin scored two goals and assisted on a third as the Senators cooled off the New York Rangers 5-2 for their first-ever home win against New York.

Sergei Zholtok, Jason Zent and Alexandre Daigle also tallied for Ottawa. Damian Rhodes stopped 19 shots for the Senators, who lost seven home games against New York since entering the league in the 1992-93 season.

New York, which came in with a five-game winning streak, lost for just the second time in its last 14 games (11-2-1). Rangers centre Wayne Gretzky was held scoreless, ending his 12-game point-scoring streak. Mark Messier tallied twice to account for the Rangers offence.

In Buffalo, Dominik Hasek made 26 saves and Dixon Ward and Donald Audette each had a goal and an assist as the Sabres extended their unbeaten streak to six games with a 5-1 victory over the Hartford Whalers in a battle between the top teams in the Northeast Division.
Anatoli Semenov, Mike Peca and Derek Plante also scored for the Sabres, who are 5-0-1 in their last six games.
Buffalo leads the Northeast by three points over Hartford and five points over third-place Pittsburgh.
In Chicago, Brett Hull scored the tying goal 9:32 into the third period as the St Louis Blues blew a three-goal lead before recovering for a 4-4 tie against the Blackhawks.

First-period goals by Joe Murphy, Hull and Craig Conroy gave the Blues a 3-0 lead, but the Blackhawks answered with four second-period tallies, capped by Sergei Krivokrasov's sixth of the season with 2:30 left for a 4-3 lead.
Bob Probert had a goal and two assists for Chicago, which played to its third straight tie.

In Uniondale, New York, Zigmund Palffy snapped a tie with a shorthanded goal as the Islanders rallied for four third-period goals in a 4-1 victory over the New Jersey Devils, who had a seven-game unbeaten streak snapped.

The Devils held a 1-0 lead entering the third period on a first-period goal by former Islander Steve Thomas, but New York defenceman Doug Houda ignited the outburst 2:10 into the period. Houda's two goals this season have come in the last two games and both have been game-tying tallies.
In Pittsburgh, Mario Lemieux's goal with 5:25 to play in the third capped a three-goal outburst in a 3:03 span as the Penguins rallied for a 3-3 tie with the Montreal Canadiens.
The goal by Lemieux gave him 1,426 points, moving him past Bryan Trottier into seventh place on the all-time list. Lemieux has scored goals in five consecutive games, netting nine goals in that span.

In Los Angeles, Philippe Boucher, Brad Smyth and Vladimir Tsyplakov scored first-period goals on consecutive shots as the Kings snapped a seven-game winless streak (0-6-1) with a 5-2 victory over the Phoenix Coyotes.
Byron Dafoe made 27 saves in a win that was costly for the Kings, who lost defenceman Rob Blake for four to six weeks with a fractured right hand.
Keith Tkachuk scored both goals for the Coyotes, who lost for just the second time in seven games.
In San Jose, Bernie Nicholls, Owen Nolan and Tony Granato all had a goal and and two assists as the Sharks pummeled the struggling Vancouver Canucks 6-1 in a Pacific Division game.
San Jose entered the game with a league-low 83 goals.
At Tampa Bay, Martin Straka scored his second goal of the game 8:06 into the third period and Dave Lowry tallied 3:26 later to give the Florida Panthers a 3-3 tie with the Lightning.
